description: How the Svelte 5 grid engine turns raw data into rendered rows: a pipeline of row models. This headless example lets you flip the group-by control and watch the pipeline change shape from core to grouped to expanded. Group rows carry an aggregate sum roll-up while leaf rows are the original objects, and the whole thing renders as a plain hand-styled <table>.

faq.question: What is a row model in SvGrid?
faq.answer: A stage in the pipeline that transforms rows: the core model wraps your data, the grouped model buckets rows by a column and inserts group rows, and the expanded model flattens the groups that are open. Features register the models they need.

faq.question: How do I compute a sum per group?
faq.answer: Set aggregate: 'sum' on the column definition. The grouped model computes the roll-up and puts it on the group row, where your markup can read and print it.

faq.question: Which features does grouping need?
faq.answer: columnGroupingFeature to build the groups and rowExpandingFeature to open and close them; the demo registers both plus rowSortingFeature and passes grouping, expanded and sorting in state. table.getRowModel().rows is the final output of the pipeline that the markup iterates.
